summary: The body is no longer pinned to 100vh on a phone, and the panes that want a viewport fraction use dvh, which tracks the browser toolbar.
modification_note: The mobile block overrode display and overflow but not height, so a phone kept a body exactly 100vh tall -- and on iOS 100vh is the viewport with the chrome hidden, which is taller than what you can see whenever the toolbar is showing. The body now grows, with min-height:100svh for the full-screen feel; .paper and .tablewrap use dvh. Every declaration is written vh-then-modern, so a browser without dvh keeps today's behaviour exactly.

edits.label: the desktop shell measures the viewport that is actually visible
on a phone the body grows instead of being pinned to 100vh
the newspaper pane tracks the toolbar instead of ignoring it
